name: @studio/app
description: Onlook: a desktop app for designing on your own codebase with an AI agent.
author: Onlook

scripts.//postinstall: Electron ships no postinstall hook, so a fresh clone has no Electron without this. `install-app-deps` is the electron-rebuild escape hatch — normally a no-op, but where a future native module gets rebuilt against Electron's ABI.
scripts.//dev:lab: The app's chrome on localhost:5273 (or the next free port; `LAB_PORT` overrides), in a browser — no Electron, `window.studio` faked (src/renderer/lab/). A design lab: anything that would touch a repo, a shell or a real agent is inert. NOT 3000, which belongs to the user's own dev server and the proof fixture.
scripts.typecheck: tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.guest.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.theme.json
scripts.//build:dmg: The raw packaging step, NOT the cut path — run `bun run build:dmg` from the repo root, which wraps this with signing-tier detection, notary credential mapping and artifact verification. `--publish never` is load-bearing: publishing is always a separate, deliberate act.

//dependencies: RUNTIME EXTERNALS ONLY — electron-builder's node-module-collector chokes on the workspace: protocol, so workspace packages live in devDependencies and Vite bundles them. Anything added here must be a real, unbundleable native/runtime module, and must be listed in electron-builder.yml's `files`/`asarUnpack`.
